implemented: The OCaml import extractor (RC15) harvests every IMPLICIT qualified value/constructor/type/field reference (e.g. `Dune_lang.parse` with no `open`) into get_imports so the dependency graph can mint inbound edges. That same full set leaked into the `imports` COMMAND, which reported 1123 'imports' for dune's pkg_rules.ml versus ~17 real directives. Added a presentation-layer filter `filter_display_imports(Vec<ImportInfo>, Language)` in crates/tldr-core/src/ast/imports.rs that, for OCaml only, drops the implicit qualified refs (identity for every other language), and wired it into the `imports` command (both the daemon-cached and direct-compute branches) in crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/imports.rs. The raw get_imports/extract_imports_from_tree output is UNCHANGED, so deps/importers/arch_rules/semantic/debt keep consuming the full set.
spike_decision: SPIKE-THEN-PATCH. The plan proposed adding an origin/kind serde field to ImportInfo (types.rs) and filtering at imports.rs:128. Investigation showed: (1) a literal struct field on types::ImportInfo cascades to ~80 construction sites across ~9 files (ast/imports.rs 42, deps.rs 21 test, resolver.rs 12 test, arch_rules.rs 2 test, plus cli output_tests + 3 integration test files) because every site uses positional struct literals, NOT `..Default::default()` — far exceeding the 2-file edit-set and the 'minimal quality' rule; (2) the imports command and its daemon path both route through get_imports, the SAME function deps/importers/arch_rules/semantic call, so the command cannot be split from those consumers without a presentation-layer change. DECISION: do NOT add a serde field. Instead identify implicit refs by the OCaml extractor's exact emission contract — they are the UNIQUE entries with is_from==Some(false) AND non-empty names (open/include => is_from Some(true) names ["*"]; module-alias => is_from Some(false) names EMPTY). This is AST-derived (reads parsed ImportInfo fields, no regex/source heuristic), zero-schema-change (perfect back-compat, strictly better than a new field), daemon-safe (operates on the deserialized Vec), and confines the core change to ast/imports.rs. The discriminator invariant is pinned by contract tests so any future extractor emission change is caught.
edit_set_deviation: Edit-set listed {crates/tldr-core/src/ast/imports.rs, crates/tldr-core/src/types.rs}. types.rs was NOT touched (the no-field design makes it unnecessary). The plan's named 'imports command PRESENTATION layer (imports.rs ~:128)' resolves to crates/tldr-cli/src/commands/imports.rs:128 (the envelope `imports: result` line) — that file was edited to call the filter. This is the plan-described presentation site, not an unanticipated dependency; it is the ONLY way to split the imports command's view from the deps/importers full-set view since both route through get_imports.
generalization_test: Symptom class = OCaml. Added 3 lib tests in ast/imports.rs: (a) test_ocaml_display_filter_drops_implicit_qualified_refs — source with 4 directives (2 open + include + module-alias) plus implicit refs across ALL FOUR path-node variants (value_path / constructor_path / type_constructor_path / field_path) and several modules; asserts raw set retains the refs (deps) while the display filter keeps exactly the 4 directives and leaks no implicit ref; (b) test_ocaml_display_filter_keeps_module_alias — pins the discriminator lower edge (module-alias has is_from Some(false) but EMPTY names => kept); (c) test_display_filter_is_identity_for_non_ocaml — proves the fix does NOT over-reach: Python/Rust/TypeScript imports (incl. `from X import a,b` with is_from+names) pass through untouched.
